declared_purpose: Local multi-agent coordination through a shared blackboard, advisory permission scoring, budget and health checks, and persistent project context. The documented workflow requires decomposition, budget checks before delegation, result verification, and sensitive-action auditing; persistent project memory is intentional (SKILL.md:86–101,145–196,200–239,525–538). Exact stored fields, archival payloads, and retention periods are implementation choices. Bundled execution uses Python standard library scripts; requirements.txt contains only documentation and commented development dependencies (requirements.txt:1–16).

data_operations.operation: Read environment selector
data_operations.source: NETWORK_AI_ENV and optional --env arguments
data_operations.data_scope: Environment name used to select local state directories.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Each script's local process; data/ or data/<env>/.
data_operations.condition: At startup. CLI overrides have the split-routing exceptions identified below.

data_operations.operation: Read, persist, and return shared coordination entries
data_operations.source: Caller-supplied keys, values, agent identifiers, and optional TTL; existing blackboard.
data_operations.data_scope: Entire markdown file is read locally. Entries contain value, source agent, timestamp, and TTL. Reads return an entry; lists return keys; snapshots return all valid entries.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Normally data[/<env>]/swarm-blackboard.md; caller-selected project-local --path is also supported. Returned data goes to the caller.
data_operations.condition: Blackboard invocation initializes and loads the file. Writes persist entries; delete removes a selected entry. Missing TTL means no expiration. Expired entries are removed during reads or persistence, without a background purge.

data_operations.operation: Stage and validate proposed changes
data_operations.source: Proposed key/value, operation, agent, TTL, and current blackboard entry.
data_operations.data_scope: Full proposed value and metadata, plus a hash of the current entry. Validation reads pending changes and can return the current entry on conflict.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Startup-selected data[/<env>]/pending_changes/<id>.pending.json; validation results go to the caller.
data_operations.condition: propose_change stages a proposal. validate_change checks current state and competing pending changes, then persists validation status.

data_operations.operation: Commit or abort, archive payload, and delete pending file
data_operations.source: Pending change record.
data_operations.data_scope: Commit applies the value or deletion to the blackboard. Both commit and abort archive the full proposal, including its value, with final status and timestamp.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Main blackboard and pending_changes/archive/<id>.committed.json or <id>.aborted.json.
data_operations.condition: Commit requires validated status. Abort does not apply the proposal. Both delete the pending file after archiving; neither path applies TTL to the archive.

data_operations.operation: Persist lock metadata and remove Windows lock markers
data_operations.source: Process identifier, current time, and marker filesystem metadata.
data_operations.data_scope: PID and acquisition timestamp; Windows marker timestamp and age.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Startup-selected data[/<env>]/.blackboard.lock and, on Windows, .blackboard.locked.
data_operations.condition: Lock acquisition writes metadata. Windows release deletes its marker, and acquisition deletes stale markers. The .blackboard.lock file itself is not deleted by release.

data_operations.operation: Score permission requests and audit requests and denials
data_operations.source: Caller-supplied agent identifier, resource label, justification, scope, and high-risk acknowledgment.
data_operations.data_scope: Derives justification quality, static identifier-based trust, risk, and approval scores. Request logs include scope, unknown-agent flag, and up to 200 justification characters plus a truncation marker; denial logs include reasons and available scores.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local permission-checker process, data[/<env>]/audit_log.jsonl, and decision output to the caller.
data_operations.condition: Every evaluated request is logged before confirmation and scoring checks. Every denial adds a separate outcome event. Identity is caller asserted; no protected external system is accessed.

data_operations.operation: Generate and persist advisory grants and signing key
data_operations.source: Approved permission request and locally generated randomness.
data_operations.data_scope: UUID-based advisory token; agent, resource, scope, restrictions, timestamps, advisory flags, and HMAC signature. A local HMAC signing key is loaded or generated.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: active_grants.json and audit_log.jsonl receive the full grant. .signing_key stores the signing key; it is not included in the grant. Issuance returns the full token to the caller.
data_operations.condition: Approval creates a five-minute grant. Key creation occurs when no readable valid key exists; owner-only chmod is attempted. CLI environment routing differs for the key, as described below.

data_operations.operation: List active grants without deleting expired records
data_operations.source: active_grants.json.
data_operations.data_scope: Agent/resource/scope, restrictions, timestamps, remaining lifetime, and masked token prefixes.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Caller output; source file remains unchanged.
data_operations.condition: --active-grants optionally filters by agent and skips expired or malformed-expiry records. The expired_cleaned output field counts skipped records rather than actual deletions.

data_operations.operation: Read shared audit history and return permission summary
data_operations.source: Entire audit_log.jsonl, including events from sibling components.
data_operations.data_scope: Permission counts grouped by agent and resource, time range, and recent events. JSON removes only the top-level details.justification field; other event details remain.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Permission-checker memory and caller output.
data_operations.condition: --audit-summary scans the whole log. Recent entries are selected across all event types; text output is narrower than JSON output.

data_operations.operation: Validate token using local grant and key
data_operations.source: Caller-supplied token, active_grants.json, and its adjacent .signing_key.
data_operations.data_scope: Grant lookup, signature verification, and expiry evaluation. Successful JSON output includes the full grant and signature-verification flag.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Validator process and caller; no persistence or deletion.
data_operations.condition: Invalid signatures and parseable expired dates are rejected. Unsigned grants, unavailable keys, and missing or unparseable expiry can still produce valid results. No agent identity authentication occurs.

data_operations.operation: Revoke or clean grants while retaining audit copies
data_operations.source: active_grants.json and optional caller-supplied token.
data_operations.data_scope: Revocation removes one grant but logs its token and full original grant. Cleanup removes parseably expired grants but logs their tokens and agent/resource/expiry metadata. JSON results contain these unmasked records.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Rewritten active_grants.json, appended audit_log.jsonl, and caller output.
data_operations.condition: Explicit token revocation or --cleanup is required. --list-expired only reads and returns records. Missing or unparseable expiry is not treated as expired.

data_operations.operation: Persist validated long-term project context and duplicate updates into audit
data_operations.source: Caller-supplied project fields, goals, stack, milestones, decisions/rationales, and banned approaches; existing context.
data_operations.data_scope: Project context and update timestamp. Initialization audits name/version; updates audit complete added or changed values. Validation checks injection patterns and size, not personal-data redaction.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: data[/<env>]/project-context.json and audit_log.jsonl.
data_operations.condition: Successful init or update. Context is intentionally persistent across sessions; the supplied commands have no context deletion or retention workflow.

data_operations.operation: Return project context for viewing or prompt insertion
data_operations.source: project-context.json.
data_operations.data_scope: show returns the full JSON. inject formats project details, goals, stack, all milestone buckets, decisions/rationales, banned approaches, and update time; it does not emit the agents section.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Caller output. Documentation instructs the caller to copy the injection block into agent system prompts.
data_operations.condition: show warns but still returns context. inject blocks on validation warnings unless --force is supplied. Prompt insertion is a separate caller action.

data_operations.operation: Load and rewrite guard tracking state
data_operations.source: Existing task, health, and budget tracking files.
data_operations.data_scope: All tasks, agents, and budget histories in three JSON objects.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Guard memory; task_tracking.json, agent_health.json, and budget_tracking.json.
data_operations.condition: Every guard construction attempts all three reads when task_tracking.json exists. Each _save_state rewrites all three. The supplied implementation does not use the separately advertised heartbeats.json or swarm_budgets.json.

data_operations.operation: Record handoff metadata and infer budget cost
data_operations.source: Task identifier, source/target agent identifiers, message, and artifact flag.
data_operations.data_scope: Stores timestamps, agent identifiers, message length, artifact flags, counts, and task status. Message content is processed for length and estimated cost, rather than stored. Interception records budget spending and allowed/blocked audit metadata.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: task_tracking.json, budget_tracking.json, audit_log.jsonl, and caller output.
data_operations.condition: record-handoff or intercept-handoff. Interception can initialize a default budget; spending and handoff recording precede the final handoff-policy decision. It does not send a message or invoke another agent.

data_operations.operation: Record heartbeats and infer agent health
data_operations.source: Caller-supplied agent, task, status, and current time.
data_operations.data_scope: First/last seen, current task, status, and counters. Health is inferred from registration and heartbeat recency, rather than confirmed agent failure.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: agent_health.json for heartbeat records; health assessments return to the caller.
data_operations.condition: heartbeat persists state. health-check treats a heartbeat older than 60 seconds as unhealthy but does not delete the record.

data_operations.operation: Persist budget history and return spending reports
data_operations.source: Task budget, description, token amounts, reasons, agent identifiers, and operation labels.
data_operations.data_scope: Budget totals, timestamps, description, and detailed spending history. Initialization duplicates the description into audit; shutdown logs its reason and may mark task status.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: budget_tracking.json, task_tracking.json when termination is recorded, audit_log.jsonl, and caller output.
data_operations.condition: Successful budget-init or budget-spend; budget-report JSON returns full spending history and aggregates. Shutdown is a local status/advisory result, not termination of an external agent.

data_operations.operation: Validate results and infer supervisory verdicts
data_operations.source: Caller-supplied result, stored agent health, handoffs, validations, and budget.
data_operations.data_scope: Checks status, required fields, confidence, output emptiness, and agent health. Persists validation time, agent, validity, and issues; error text can be copied into issues. Ordinary output content is not persisted by validation.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: task_tracking.json when the task exists; assessments and supervisory verdicts return to the caller.
data_operations.condition: validate-result or supervisor-review. Contrary to the documented automatic result audit events, this validation path saves tracking state without appending result_validated/result_rejected to audit_log.jsonl.

data_operations.operation: Require caller-managed logging of sensitive actions
data_operations.source: Caller-performed sensitive action and supplied action metadata.
data_operations.data_scope: Example includes timestamp, action, agent, description, and justification without truncation or redaction.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: The example appends to {baseDir}/data/audit_log.jsonl.
data_operations.condition: Documentation requires every sensitive action to be logged; the manual example executes only if followed by the caller and does not implement environment routing.

data_operations.operation: Describe conditional host-platform delegation
data_operations.source: Caller-created task instructions, relevant context, constraints, expected output, and optionally returned project context.
data_operations.data_scope: Delegated task payload and prompt context.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Named agents through host-platform tools; external model APIs may be involved, but providers and storage are unspecified.
data_operations.condition: Caller follows the documented workflow after a budget allowance. The bundled Python scripts do not implement this transfer; ordinary script returns can remain with their caller.

data_operations.operation: Include existing coordination records in the public package
data_operations.source: Packaged root swarm-blackboard.md.
data_operations.data_scope: Authentication-related source paths, agent/reviewer identifiers, review comments, test metrics, infrastructure configuration, and timestamps; all four entries have null TTL.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: The public skill package's root swarm-blackboard.md.
data_operations.condition: Already present in the supplied package. The Python default points to data[/<env>]/swarm-blackboard.md; loading this root artifact requires selecting its path. Its provenance is unknown.

potential_excess.data_scope: Full committed or aborted proposal values and associated agent metadata.
potential_excess.condition: Every successful commit or abort; archives have no TTL enforcement.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Atomic coordination requires staging and conflict checking. Archiving full payloads is an implementation choice, separate from maintaining an outcome audit.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Keep the proposal until resolution and apply the committed value with its intended lifetime.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Archive outcome metadata and a change identifier/hash; omit resolved payloads or give payload archives an explicit short retention period.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Retain any payload genuinely needed for an authorized recovery window; preserve conflict checks and commit/abort traceability.

potential_excess.data_scope: Task results, cached values, and coordination entries with omitted TTL.
potential_excess.condition: write/propose accepts absent TTL; null TTL never expires. Expiration otherwise requires subsequent access or persistence.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The entry document describes the blackboard as TTL-scoped coordination memory, while project context supplies intentional long-term memory.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Keep shared results available through verification and synthesis.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Add task-lifecycle deletion or suitable default TTLs for ephemeral entries, plus explicit cleanup of expired entries.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Allow deliberate longer retention for unfinished tasks; preserve authorized persistent project knowledge in project context.

potential_excess.data_scope: Full advisory token identifiers, signatures, and duplicated original grant records.
potential_excess.condition: Grant issuance logs the complete signed grant; revocation logs the full original grant; cleanup logs expired token identifiers.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Sensitive-action auditing is explicitly required. Full token/signature duplication is extra data in that required action, rather than a reason to remove the audit event.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Retain attributable grant, denial, revocation, and cleanup outcomes; keep live verification material in active grant storage.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Use a non-authorizing correlation identifier in audit records and omit full token values and signatures; retain necessary agent/resource/scope/outcome metadata.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve reliable event correlation and live token validation. These tokens are advisory, not external service credentials.

potential_excess.data_scope: Expired grant records, including tokens, scope, agent, restrictions, and signature.
potential_excess.condition: Expiry does not delete records. Active listing skips them; removal requires explicit revocation or cleanup.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Advisory grants have a five-minute validity period; retaining complete expired live-state records is not required for validation.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Reject expired grants and preserve a minimized lifecycle audit.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Prune expired records during routine grant maintenance or provide an explicit bounded cleanup lifecycle.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep unexpired grants and necessary audit metadata; do not confuse expiry or file removal with deletion of audit copies.

potential_excess.data_scope: Justification prefixes, complete project-context changes, budget descriptions, and manually supplied descriptive text.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: audit_log.jsonl, separate from the operational context or budget files.
potential_excess.condition: Permission requests, context updates, budget initialization, or caller-managed manual logging. Permission justification truncation does not redact sensitive content; it does not apply to sibling components.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Audit events and meaningful business justification are required; unlimited duplication of raw project or task content is an implementation choice.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Record who changed or requested what, the outcome, and a sufficient non-sensitive rationale.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Use reviewed concise rationales, structured purpose/change identifiers, field names and hashes; redact unnecessary sensitive substrings before audit persistence.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep full authorized project notes in project-context.json where needed, and preserve enough audit detail for attribution and investigation.

potential_excess.data_scope: Recent non-permission events, full grant records, and context update payloads preserved after justification-only redaction.
potential_excess.condition: Recent shared-log entries contain these fields. Selection includes all event types, and redaction removes only details.justification.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: This command declares a permission-summary purpose: counts, per-agent/resource breakdowns, and recent permission activity.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Return accurate permission aggregates and relevant recent permission outcomes.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Filter recent activity to permission events and allowlist summary fields; mask token identifiers and omit signatures and unrelated context payloads.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep denial counting based on explicit denial events. Treat this as narrowing a caller return, not as preventing an observed remote disclosure.

potential_excess.data_scope: Accumulating handoff/validation histories, error text, task associations, budget descriptions, and free-text spending reasons.
potential_excess.condition: Records persist across guard runs without a supplied task-finalization or retention cleanup path.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Budget enforcement, health checks, and supervisory review need working task state; permanent detailed histories are distinct from intentional persistent project memory.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Preserve current counters, recent health, and evidence needed for an unfinished task's review.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Add a task-finish retention policy, compact old histories into necessary aggregates, unlink stale task associations, and store structured validation errors instead of unnecessary raw error text.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Do not purge state needed for ongoing supervision, budget enforcement, or an expressly authorized diagnostic window.

potential_excess.data_scope: Full proposed values and their agent/change metadata.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Startup environment's pending_changes/ and archive/, instead of the CLI-selected environment's directories.
potential_excess.condition: blackboard.py --env differs from NETWORK_AI_ENV or the startup default. --env changes args.path but leaves PENDING_DIR and LOCK_PATH unchanged.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Environment selection is explicitly presented as state isolation. Staging proposals is necessary, but persisting them across the selected environment boundary is not.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Keep proposal, validation, commit, archive, and locking state consistent with the selected blackboard environment.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Resolve the environment once and pass its pending directory and lock path into the blackboard instance.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep atomic coordination within each environment; handle existing misplaced pending records explicitly.

potential_excess.data_scope: HMAC signing-key access and use across environment boundaries.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Permission-checker process reads or creates the startup environment's .signing_key while grants and audit records target the CLI-selected environment.
potential_excess.condition: check_permission.py --env differs from the startup environment and issuance reaches signing. --env changes GRANTS_FILE/AUDIT_LOG but not _DATA_DIR used by the signer.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Local grant integrity requires signing, while documented environment isolation calls for separate state. Access to another environment's key is avoidable.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Sign and validate a grant using its selected environment's key.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Derive the signing key and directory creation from the resolved GRANTS_FILE parent, consistently with validate_token.py.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Provide a compatibility plan for existing grants signed using the previous routing. No raw key disclosure is shown.

potential_excess.data_scope: Operational-looking source paths, review comments, agent identifiers, test metrics, infrastructure settings, and timestamps.
potential_excess.condition: These records are included in the supplied package, with null TTL. Whether they are real operational records or synthetic examples is unresolved.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: A reusable orchestration skill needs a state schema or example, rather than these particular task records.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Provide an initial blackboard structure and demonstrate supported entry shapes.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Ship an empty template or clearly synthetic minimal examples.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve the documented format; establish provenance before characterizing this as exposure of real project data.

unknowns: End-to-end remote disclosure remains unresolved: host delegation and prompt insertion may use external model APIs, but supplied source identifies no provider, exact transmitted envelope, attached conversation history, retention, or deletion behavior.

skill.json declares delegation, spawning, swarm queries, traces, and broad state-return interfaces, but their host adapters and the separate TypeScript engine are absent. Metadata alone does not establish execution or data capture.
Actual runtime inputs and state are unavailable. The root blackboard's provenance is unknown, so its records cannot be classified as real personal or confidential project data.
Downstream enforcement of advisory grants, real sensitive-system access, and caller-managed sensitive-action logging cannot be verified from the bundled scripts.

Filesystem readership, effective access permissions, backups, and external copies are unspecified. Local deletion shown here does not establish erasure from archives, audit logs, backups, or host-platform storage.
